title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-10-13
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Samplitude Professional v9.11 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Impeccable soundboard capture of a brilliant 1968 show featuring a smoking Dark Star, an epic Eleven, and a stellar Other One>Cryptical.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as crystal‑clear and well‑balanced, typical of the Charlie Miller soundboard source. Musically the concert shines with a near‑perfect Dark Star, an incendiary The Eleven (highlighting both Jerry and Phil), and a thrilling Other One→Cryptical sequence, while the first set generally outshines a more uneven second set.

ai_rating.rationale: Five‑star praise dominates (four 5‑star and one 4‑star), with strong comments on both performance and recording quality; only minor criticism of the second set keeps the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners note a clean, well‑balanced mix with no major glitches; all available copies are reported as good quality, and the Charlie Miller version is specifically lauded.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is praised as superior, with tight transitions and high energy; the second set contains a jarring splice from New Potato into Drums and ends with mellow feedback/space, making it feel less cohesive.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers highlight his masterful guitar tone on Dark Star and Death Don't Have No Mercy, calling his playing top‑notch.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass work is described as feeding off the band and delivering powerful moments, especially during The Eleven.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal contribution on The Eleven is singled out as a standout moment, even though he was reportedly considered for removal from the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drummers are called fabulous early on (especially in The Eleven) but the later Drums segment is deemed less interesting.
